findings: Serialized terminal writes and coalesced settlement avoid overlapping sweeps; failures stop a bounded batch and use monotonic backoff.
Failed binding retains the exact acquired lease; new admission remains fenced while that lease is unresolved.
Request work is bounded before parsing/lookup, with per-owner limits and separate observation/subscription allowances. Before-lookup overload retains unknown classification.
Late pre-exhaustion sibling success cannot substitute for a post-cooldown probe; transient-failure state is checkpointed.
SDK tool starts are bounded and stop after save failure/cancellation; capacity deadlines survive restoration and early clicks do not spend another attempt.
Error and presentation contracts both expose wait; exhausted turn budget takes precedence over a wait/compaction hint.
Clarified asynchronous engine terminal persistence: a completed stream does not prove the receipt/settlement committed. New admission still blocks while terminal writes are unconfirmed.
Preserved original first-pass evidence; installed r2 runtimes retain closed gates and account state, with SDK/public application rollout separate.

Read-only schema authority review confirms old-epoch settlement remains tied to the original lease binding. No SQL or privilege changes were made. Supabase changelog/connection guidance inspected; no applicable connection/API migration was introduced.
